diet.note: An inference from anatomy, not from gut contents. Alvarezsauroids have short, strong forelimbs suited to digging, consistent with eating insects such as ants and termites (Leedham et al. 2026; NHM). Choiniere et al. 2021 found Shuvuuia's eyes and ears suited to hunting at night. PBDB lists it simply as a carnivore.

timeRange.note: PBDB dates S. deserti occurrences (Djadokhta Formation, Mongolia) only to the Campanian; the Ma values are the ICS v2024/12 Campanian stage boundaries. NHM gives 81-75 Ma.

text.en: Shuvuuia was a tiny desert dinosaur from Mongolia, about 60 centimetres long, living roughly 84 to 72 million years ago. Its name means 'bird'. Its relatives, the alvarezsauroids, had short, strong arms suited to digging, so scientists think it may have eaten insects such as termites. Its large eyes and owl-like ears suggest it hunted at night.
Shuvuuia's inner ear suggests its hearing rivalled that of a barn owl, and its eyes were suited to very low light.

uncertain.note: Insectivory is inferred from alvarezsauroid anatomy (Leedham et al. 2026; NHM); there is no direct evidence such as gut contents.
No published mass estimate found in the sources checked.
